learningObjectives.title: Climate change: causes, effects and responses

questions.q: The enhanced greenhouse effect leads to global warming because greenhouse gases:
options: Trap more outgoing heat in the atmosphere
questions.explain: Extra greenhouse gases trap more long-wave radiation, warming the planet.

questions.q: A major human cause of climate change is:
questions.explain: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, a key greenhouse gas.
Carbon dioxide and methane are important greenhouse gases.

questions.q: A likely effect of climate change is:
options: Rising sea levels and more extreme weather
questions.explain: Warming causes ice melt, thermal expansion of oceans and more extreme events.

questions.q: 'Mitigation' of climate change means actions that:
options: Reduce the causes, e.g. cutting emissions
questions.explain: Mitigation tackles causes (e.g. renewable energy); adaptation copes with effects.

questions.q: Deforestation contributes to climate change because trees:
options: Absorb carbon dioxide, so removing them raises CO2 levels
questions.explain: Forests are carbon sinks; deforestation releases stored carbon and reduces absorption.

questions.q: Switching from coal power to wind and solar is an example of:
questions.explain: Renewable energy cuts greenhouse-gas emissions, a mitigation strategy.

questions.q: Building flood defences and drought-resistant crops are examples of:
questions.explain: Adaptation manages the impacts of a changing climate.

questions.q: In a food chain, producers are usually:
questions.explain: Producers make their own food and form the base of the food chain.

options: A network of interconnected food chains
questions.explain: Food webs show the many feeding relationships in an ecosystem.
Biotic = living; abiotic = non-living (climate, soil, water).

questions.q: 'Sustainable management' of a resource means using it in a way that:
options: Meets present needs without harming future generations
Uses it up as fast as possible
questions.explain: Sustainability balances present use with long-term availability.
Renewables (solar, wind, hydro) are replenished naturally, unlike fossil fuels.

questions.q: Removing a top predator from a food web can cause:
options: Populations lower in the web to change, affecting the whole ecosystem
questions.explain: Ecosystems are interdependent, so one change can have knock-on effects.

questions.q: A community wants sustainable timber. A suitable approach is:
questions.explain: Sustainable forestry maintains the resource for the future.

questions.q: International agreements to cut emissions are needed because climate change is:
options: Not caused by humans at all
questions.explain: Emissions anywhere affect the whole planet, so global action is required.
